title: Federal pesticide measurement is fitted to one farming system
subtitle: Share of a county's cropland that sits inside the NASS Agricultural Chemical Use Program's published 2013-2025 frame, by how diversified that county's cropland is. Coverage peaks at 92% on the two-crop corn-soybean rotation and falls away in both directions.

x.label: Crop diversity of the county (effective number of crops, exp(Shannon) of acreage shares)
x.note: One point per decile of counties, positioned at the decile's median. Deciles are equal-count (295-296 counties each), not equal-width; eff_crops_min / eff_crops_max give each decile's true span and may be drawn as horizontal whiskers.

y.label: Share of the county's census crop acres inside the published survey frame

series.label: Cropland inside the federal pesticide-use survey frame, 2013-2025
series.point_size_note: Size each decile's marker by `acres` (6.1M to 42.4M) so the reader can see that the peak decile is also the largest block of cropland in the country.

series.label: Share of those same acres in hay and haylage - a crop never once surveyed
series.axis: same y-axis (both are shares of the same acreage), drawn subordinate to the primary series

annotations.text: Peak coverage: 92%. Effective crops 2.11-2.38 - a corn-soybean rotation. 42.4M acres, the single largest block of US cropland.
Least diverse counties: 5.8% coverage. 95% of their cropland is hay - grown by 612,946 farms, a third of all US farms, and never surveyed for pesticide use in 36 years.
Most diverse counties: 58.9%. Mixed fruit, vegetable and forage systems fall outside the frame crop by crop.

Not a monotone decline. Spearman rho = +0.272 across counties, but the curve is an inverted U: the instrument is not biased against complexity in general, it is tuned to one cropping system. Shape holds under all three coverage definitions (cov_ever, cov_recent_us) in the same file.
12 states have zero coverage (AK CT DE HI MA MD NH NV RI UT VT WV); WY 4.4%, NJ 8.5%. Illinois 97%, Iowa 95%.

source_note: USDA NASS QuickStats bulk, mirrored 2026-09-14: qs.environmental_20260912.txt.gz (Agricultural Chemical Use Program, SOURCE_DESC=SURVEY, DOMAIN_DESC~CHEMICAL, 1990-2025) and qs.census2022.txt.gz (2022 Census of Agriculture, SECTOR_DESC=CROPS). 2,951 counties with >=1,000 census crop acres, 302.1M acres = 98.8% of the national crop base. Coverage = a crop acre counts as measured only if NASS published a chemical-use estimate for that commodity in that county's own state. Computed by analysis/mendez/compute.py.

optional_background_layer.marks: scatter, 2,951 points, x = eff_crops, y = cov_recent, very low opacity
optional_background_layer.purpose: Shows the dispersion behind the decile line - counties pile up at 0 and at 1. Include only if it does not obscure the primary line.
